lessons.title: -हून (-hūn) — from
lessons.gloss: from — the ending that answers the second question of every spoken interview

segments.text: Chapter twenty-three taught शहर as a line on a form. A form wants the name of a city. An interviewer wants something else.

segments.instruction: say -ne, then -śī, and name which one takes a person
segments.source: [YOU RECALL: say *-ne*, then *-śī*, and name which one takes a person]

segments.text: -हून — -hūn — from.
मी पुण्याहून येतो. — mī puṇyāhūn yeto. — I come from Pune.

That sentence is the second thing said in almost every spoken A1 interview, and until this lesson the book could write शहर: पुणे on a form and not say it out loud. A form field is a label; -हून (-hūn) is an answer.
The stem is the one you already bend: पुणे becomes पुण्या-, then -हून (-hūn), no space. And because इथे and तिथे are place words too, they take it and give you two more:
इथून — ithūn — from here तिथून — tithūn — from there.
Notice what happened to the shape: इथे ends in -ए and the ending replaced it, exactly as it does on पुणे. The rule you learned in chapter forty-one is doing all the work.

segments.instruction: mī puṇyāhūn yeto — I come from Pune
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *mī puṇyāhūn yeto* — I come from Pune]

segments.instruction: ithūn, then tithūn — from here, from there
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *ithūn*, then *tithūn* — from here, from there]

segments.prompt: Say that you come from Pune, then from here.

feedback.correct: An origin, said rather than filled in.
feedback.incorrect: puṇe bends to puṇyā-; ithe drops its -e for -ūn.

segments.text: What can you now say that a form field could not? (I come from Pune — an answer, not a label.) What does इथे become with it? (इथून.)
Sources: Wiktionary: हून.

lessons.title: पासून (pāsūn) — from, since
lessons.gloss: from, since — the starting point of a journey and of a stretch of time, in one word

segments.text: -हून (-hūn) says where a journey began. It does not say when one did.
पासून — pāsūn — from, since.
उद्यापासून — udyāpāsūn — from tomorrow onwards.

पासून (pāsūn) is written joined, like -हून (-hūn), and takes the same oblique stem. What makes it worth its own lesson is that it works on time as well as place — Marathi uses one word where English splits from and since, and a Marathi speaker feels no difference between the start of a road and the start of a week.
Against -हून (-hūn) the contrast is direction of attention. -हून (-hūn) looks back at the place you LEFT; पासून (pāsūn) looks forward from a starting point that is still running:
पुण्याहून — I came from Pune, and I am elsewhere now. उद्यापासून — starting tomorrow, and continuing.
That is why a notice about opening hours uses पासून (pāsūn) and a traveller uses -हून (-hūn).

segments.prompt: Say 'from tomorrow' and 'from Pune', and name which one is about time.

feedback.correct: One starts a stretch, the other names a source.
feedback.incorrect: pāsūn does time and a running start; -hūn names where you left.

segments.text: Which of the two also does TIME? (पासून (pāsūn).) Which one looks back at where you left? (-हून (-hūn).)
Sources: Wiktionary: पासून (pāsūn).

lessons.title: कुठून (kuṭhūn) — from where
lessons.gloss: from where — the interview's opening question, built out of two things you already own

segments.text: You can answer I come from Pune. Nobody has asked you yet.
कुठून — kuṭhūn — from where.
तुम्ही कुठून येता? — tumhī kuṭhūn yetā? — where are you from?

Nothing here is new except the answer to a question you can now finally ask. कुठून (kuṭhūn) is कुठे with -हून (-hūn) on it, and the -ए dropped for -ऊ in exactly the way इथे became इथून two lessons ago. A place word, an ablative, and the same rule.
Its position obeys chapter thirty-eight: an asking word stands in the answer's own slot, so कुठून (kuṭhūn) sits precisely where पुण्याहून would sit and nothing moves to the front.
तुम्ही पुण्याहून येता. becomes तुम्ही कुठून (kuṭhūn) येता?
Now put the whole family beside each other, because they are one shape with three stems and you have owned two of them since chapter forty:
कुठून (kuṭhūn) from where, इथून from here, तिथून from there.

segments.instruction: tumhī kuṭhūn yetā? — and answer it about yourself
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *tumhī kuṭhūn yetā?* — and answer it about yourself]

segments.instruction: the three together — kuṭhūn, ithūn, tithūn

segments.prompt: Ask where somebody is from, then answer with Pune.
acceptedResponses: tumhī kuṭhūn yetā? — mī puṇyāhūn yeto
तुम्ही कुठून येता? मी पुण्याहून येतो

feedback.incorrect: kuṭhūn takes the slot puṇyāhūn would take; nothing moves.

segments.text: What two pieces is कुठून (kuṭhūn) made of? (कुठे plus -हून (-hūn).) Where in the sentence does it stand? (Where the answer would stand.)

lessons.title: Answer the second interview question
lessons.gloss: the interview's second exchange, asked and answered without a form

segments.text: Say the question and its answer as one exchange, both halves aloud.

segments.instruction: tumhī kuṭhūn yetā? — then answer it
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *tumhī kuṭhūn yetā?* — then answer it]

segments.instruction: udyāpāsūn — and hear that this one is a time
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *udyāpāsūn* — and hear that this one is a time]

segments.instruction: say देणे and its root — deṇe, from the ancient deh₃-, "to give"
segments.source: [YOU RECALL: say **देणे** and its root — *deṇe*, from the ancient *deh₃-*, "to give"]

segments.prompt: Ask where somebody is from, answer it, then say from tomorrow onwards.
acceptedResponses: tumhī kuṭhūn yetā? — mī puṇyāhūn yeto. udyāpāsūn.
तुम्ही कुठून येता? मी पुण्याहून येतो उद्यापासून

feedback.correct: A place left, and a time starting.
feedback.incorrect: -hūn for the source, pāsūn for the stretch.

segments.text: Which form field can you now turn into a spoken answer? (शहर — मी पुण्याहून येतो.) Which of the two endings also does time? (पासून (pāsūn).)
